qs.q:
Laptops instead of textbooks — Which person thinks that…

A=Annabelle (textbooks should remain, highlight with pen, laptops cause injuries and addiction)
B=Bradley (laptops as supplements, not replacement; parents should insure school laptops; laptops have limits e.g. power cuts)
C=Cheryl (reduce back injuries but kids misuse laptops; teachers rarely use laptops; everyone learns differently)
D=Dominic (digital revolution cannot be turned back; parents should purchase their own laptops; teachers need training)
E=Elaine (information changes quickly; students not mature enough; tools to minimise distractions; online homework reduces socialising)
F=Forrest (kids hate hauling textbooks; cost of maintaining networks cancels benefits; sometimes textbook is quicker)

0. students often damage their laptops? [C=Cheryl]
1. laptops should be used as an additional learning tool?
2. getting rid of textbooks would change teaching methods?
3. despite being heavy, textbooks are still useful?
4. the budget for laptop maintenance is bigger than for textbooks?
5. too much time on laptops can cause health issues?
6. children will need help to stay focused while working with laptops?
7. the use of laptops could result in withdrawal from peers?
8. the traditional approach to learning will die out?
9. finding information in a textbook can be quicker than on a laptop?
10. getting rid of textbooks would disadvantage some students?
11. students should own their laptops?
12. you cannot always depend on laptops?
items: 1 — laptops should be used as an additional learning tool?
2 — getting rid of textbooks would change teaching methods?
3 — despite being heavy, textbooks are still useful?
4 — the budget for laptop maintenance is bigger than for textbooks?
5 — too much time on laptops can cause health issues?
6 — children will need help to stay focused while working with laptops?
7 — the use of laptops could result in withdrawal from peers?
8 — the traditional approach to learning will die out?
9 — finding information in a textbook can be quicker than on a laptop?
10 — getting rid of textbooks would disadvantage some students?
12 — you cannot always depend on laptops?

Romantic Fiction

"You can be exposed to suffering and heartache, but they don't belong to you, they are someone else's pain. And you know that, DESPITE THE OBSTACLES, LOVE WILL WIN OUT."

Why does the author like romantic novels?
A They are better than friends.
B They always have a happy ending.
C They make you feel heartache.

opts: They always have a happy ending.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"I am a big fan of ESCAPISM. No matter how difficult our own lives might be, a GOOD STORY CAN PUSH ALL OUR TROUBLES AWAY."

What does the author think about the effects of romantic fiction?
A They are equally good and bad.
B Reading romantic fiction can be dangerous.
C Escapism helps us put up with our lives.
D Romantic novels can help you find love.
opts: They are equally good and bad.
Reading romantic fiction can be dangerous.
Escapism helps us put up with our lives.
Romantic novels can help you find love.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"Most important for me is that the characters are easy for us to IDENTIFY WITH. We want to be able to RELATE with what happens to them, which SHOULD REFLECT OUR OWN LIVES."

What does the author say about the characters in romantic novels?
A They should have ordinary experiences.
B They should possess strong identities.
C They should keep journals.
D They should include some sensible men.
opts: They should include some sensible men.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"Reading romantic fiction is the equivalent of EATING A BOWL OF YOUR FAVOURITE POTATO CHIPS while watching your favourite programme. It might not be NUTRITIOUS but a part of you CANNOT RESIST IT."

According to the author, why is romantic fiction popular with women?
A It is reassuringly familiar.
B It is a pleasurable experience.
C They like the male heroes.
D They don't want to think too hard.
opts: They don't want to think too hard.

qs.q:
Manchester – a city never lost for words

"Linguists at the University of Manchester have discovered their city has a population that speaks at least 153 languages. (19) ____. Research conducted by professor Yaron Matras suggests the true figure could be even higher."

A This has consequently prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and the arrival of overseas students to the city.
C It may have substantially underestimated the number of multilingual households across the UK.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester as it tends to have very established communities.
E It could have helped to forge the city's linguistic and cultural diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places linguistically.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs at the level of public services.
H This huge ratio indicates just how deeply rooted and firmly established its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C — It may have underestimated the number of multilingual households.
D — Still less diverse than Manchester.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places linguistically.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
